Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

within preposition

a time: before it is out

also within a week, within two days, in less than, in the next few days, in a few days

classical

Plaut. Curc. 448: subēgit sōlus intrā vīgintī diēs
Liv. 36.10.1: intrā decimum diem quam Pherās vēnerat

intrā + acc.

preposition with the accusative

within, in less than (a time)

Sets the limit: before the time is out. With quam, within so many days of an event (Liv. 36.10.1, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • 1bīduum: long i (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked (s.v. biduus)). As in trīduum, which Lewis & Short marks long. De Vaan 173, s.v. diū: the long ī of bīduum, trīduum, which Walde–Hofmann explain from postrīdiē and de Vaan perhaps from bīmus.

    cāsus ablātīvus1 — in, within (the time something takes)

    construction: the length of time in the ablative, with no preposition · classical · Cic. Att. 9.14.2: quicquid est bīduō sciēmus; Cic. Fam. 7.4: mē hōc bīduō aut trīduō exspectā

    The everyday way in Cicero’s letters: paucīs diēbus, in a few days; hōc bīduō, in the next two days. It answers “how soon?”; intrā stresses that the time will not be overrun.

Examples

  • dīmidiam partem nātiōnum ūsque omnium subēgit sōlus intrā vīgintī diēs

    single-handed, within twenty days, he conquered half of all the nations there arePlaut. Curc. 447–448

  • Cūrā igitur ut valeās, et mē hōc bīduō aut trīduō exspectā.

    So take care of your health, and expect me within the next two or three days.Cic. Fam. 7.4

  • quicquid est bīduō sciēmus

    whatever it is, we shall know within two daysCic. Att. 9.14.2

  • sed nunc properō. perscrībam ad tē paucīs diēbus omnia.

    But I am in a hurry now; I’ll write you the whole story in a few days.Cic. Att. 5.17.2

See also inside, for, during, in … days’ time, few.
